recipes.name: Easy Company Chicken
ingredients_raw: 2 (10.5 ounce) cans condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Place chicken into a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Mix condensed soup, Parmesan, mayonnaise, and curry powder together in a bowl until well combined; pour over chicken.

Cover and bake in the preheated oven for 25 minutes. Uncover and continue to bake until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, 10 to 15 more minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Company Chicken
raw_recipe.description: It's five-ingredient company chicken to the rescue when last minute guests arrive! Parmesan is a secret ingredient in this creamy curried chicken you whip up in a jiffy.

review.reviewBody: I should have mentioned the chicken soup can be switched or combined with either cream of mushroom, cream of broccoli, or cream of celery soup. I personally use the low fat cream of chicken mixed with the low fat cream of celery.-casch

Very well received by my family. Only had cr of mushroom and cr of celery soup. Used Dukes mayo and put in about 1/2 c chicken broth. 2 teaspoons hot Madeira curry seasoning and threw it in the instapot with 3 chopped up (because they were fresh out of freezer) chicken breasts. After instapot cycle finished I put 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese in the mix and then placed in a 9x9 casserole dish put another 1/2 cup grated Parmesan on top and cooked uncovered in oven for 15 min trying to brown it up. That did not work so probably won’t bother next time. Very moist with mild flavor but good and served over rice.

It is a good recipe. I would just say that it would be best to half the chicken before putting in the casserole dish and/or increase cook time and/or temperature. I cooked these at the recommended temperature (350) for nearly 50 minutes and the chicken was no where near done. I ended up with another 20 minutes at 350 and then another 15 at 380. Then I left the cover on so they could continue to cook but not overcook. Next time, I'll cut the breasts in half and start with 45 min at 380 and play around with it from there.

This was great!! I cut the chicken into bite sized pieces. I used a smaller dish (8x8) so I had to cook it almost an hour. Next time I won't do that!

I read the reviews first so I used 1 can of soup (cream of chicken and mushroom) and 8oz of chicken broth. I also added a little garlic powder, onion powder and black pepper, and I used a lot more curry, almost 3tsp.

I served it with rice and steamed broccoli, we ate it all up. Thanks!

I used one can of cream of chicken and one can of cream of mushroom, and substituted shredded mozzerella because that's what I had. I was hoping it wouldn't be too spicy, since my husband is not a huge fan of curry, but it turned out deliciously creamy and mild. I also upped the cooking time to 1 hr 20 min, since my chicken was not completely thawed. It tasted great with brown rice!

Yummy and a nice change of pace from the regular old chicken dinner. I love curry, and even though I made it with 3 tsp it could have used a bit more. Otherwise I made it pretty close to the recipe...maybe a little less mayo and soup. I thought about putting the chicken broth/stock in, but thought I would try it without the first time. It was thick and we liked it. My husband would have preferred it over noodles but I loved the brown rice with it. I cut the chicken into long strips which made it easy to flip in the oven and also looked nice when serving propped up on a bed of rice. Served it with broccoli. I will make this again and try a couple other variations based on other reviews.

I made this with only cream of mushroom soup since I didn't have cream of chicken. Followed the recipe otherwise, and tasted the sauce before putting over the chicken... and ended up adding another teaspoon of curry to it. I don't usually like curry, but this was pretty good, and my curry crazy husband loved it and has asked me to make it on a regular basis. I agree with other reviewers in that this is not really a pretty enough presentation to be a company dish, but it tastes good, all the same. Using the two cans of soup gave me plenty of sauce to spoon over the chicken and some rice when it was all done. Update: I've made this several times now, and I have to say that cream of chicken puts it over the top! I won't make it with mushroom anymore. I use one can of soup, as two is too much sauce. I just about double the curry and leave the parm the same. Great served with the sauce over steamed potatoes!

I made a few changes to this recipe after reading reviews. Our family enjoyed it tonight. My two year old gobbled it up and the rest of us liked it pretty much. Here are the changes I made. I used one can of cream of mushroom soup, 2 tsp. curry powder and 2/3 can of chicken broth. The chicken, cheese and mayo stayed the same. It made lots of gravy that was great for spooning over rice. I also cut up the chicken into strips before cooking. I will use this recipe again. Thanks!

My entire family LOVED this meal! My 4 yr. old exclaimed- "this is better than pizza!" I doubled the curry and replaced one can of crm. of chicken for crm. of celery. I also cut up the chicken into bite sized pieces before cooking. I served it over rice with some broccoli and rolls, it was super easy and so tastey! This is the best meal that I've found on this site! Thanx!

One of my favorites! My mom makes this and it was one of the first meals I made. It’s so easy too! I’m 25 now, making it tonight for the hundredth time. I’ve made this as SO many first meals that I’ve cooked for different people and everyone’s ALWAYS loved it! I’m so sad to see any bad reviews! I make this with jasmine rice. Yummy!

YUM! I poached 3 bone in chicken breasts (instead of baking boneless). I used 1 can cream of chicken/mushroom (blend) soup and 1 can cream of chicken - as other reviews mentioned, too much cream of chicken flavor to use alone. Mixed it all up, baked it and served over rice. Everyone cleaned their plates! Thanks for the great recipe casch!
Definitely needed more curry than recommended! Really liked this!
Done since 2010 or earlier. The best never go away.
My family loves this! Have been making it for years! Easy, creamy and always a hit with the kids. We serve over white rice with broccoli or green beans on the side.
I really enjoyed this. I added more curry because I like the taste of curry. Really good though.

This is a respectable dish for something that is so easy but I thought it could use just a little more jazz. As usual for me, I cut the chicken breasts into medallions which works out perfectly for my family. This was great served over rice.
Meh, wasn't great, but it wasn't the worst thing we've ever eaten either. I think there was WAY to much sauce. If I make it again I will only use 1 can of soup and will have to cook longer.
Yes we loved it I put one can of mushrooms 4oz. I served it over brown rice. Megan
I loved this recipe! Even my Husband liked it and he's a Executive Chef and is very picky. I forgot the curry powder but, it still came out fantastic. Ill definitely be making this again.

This is pretty good, but not fabulous. I would have rated only 3 stars, but my 8 year old daughter gobbled it up, which is rare, so that has some merit. I halved the sauce ingredients and still had plenty to cover the chicken.
